body.statement: For any \(S,T\subseteq[n]\), all projectors below act on the fixed space \(\mathbb R^n\), and \[\left\|P_{\operatorname{span}\{A^{-\top}e_j:j\in T\}}P_{\operatorname{span}\{A^{-\top}e_j:j\in S\}^{\perp}}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad T\subseteq S.\] For every witness label \(i\in T\setminus S\), the left-hand side is at least \(\rho_i(G)=1/(\|A^{-\top}e_i\|_2\|Ae_i\|_2)=1/(\|H^{\top}e_i\|_2\|Ge_i\|_2)>0\), and hence at least \(\rho^{\ast}(G)\). The source's printed quantity \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)=\min_i\|H_{i,:}\|_2\|G_{:,i}\|_2\) is a norm product, not this reciprocal lower bound.
body.justification: The graph transcript needs a correct zero-versus-positive projector characterization under nonorthogonal mixing.
body.gap: The printed norm-product expression in the closest source can exceed one and a subset-pseudoinverse identity used with it is false; this proposition uses dual vectors and actual projector geometry.
body.consumer: It prevents false edge decisions in the population proof and supplies the geometric quantity to be enclosed numerically.
body.proof_tex:
Because \(A=U^{\top}G\) is invertible under \(\mathrm{ass{:}full\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}mixing}\), define
\(h_i=A^{-\top}e_i\) and \(g_i=Ae_i\).  They are dual:
\[
 h_i^{\top}g_j=e_i^{\top}A^{-1}Ae_j=\mathbf 1\{i=j\}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal U_T=\operatorname{span}\{h_i:i\in T\}\) and
\(\mathcal W_S=\operatorname{span}\{h_i:i\in S\}^{\perp}\).  If \(T\subseteq S\), then \(\mathcal U_T\subseteq\mathcal W_S^{\perp}\), so
\(P_{\mathcal U_T}P_{\mathcal W_S}=0\).  Conversely, take \(i\in T\setminus S\).  Duality gives \(g_i\in\mathcal W_S\), whereas \(h_i\in\mathcal U_T\).  Testing the projector product on \(g_i/\|g_i\|_2\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|P_{\mathcal U_T}P_{\mathcal W_S}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\ge \left\|P_{\mathcal U_T}\frac{g_i}{\|g_i\|_2}\right\|_2\\
 &\ge \left|\left\langle
       \frac{h_i}{\|h_i\|_2},\frac{g_i}{\|g_i\|_2}
       \right\rangle\right|
 =\frac{1}{\|A^{-\top}e_i\|_2\|Ae_i\|_2}>0.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the equivalence and the stated witness bound.  Since \(U\) is an isometry from \(\mathbb R^n\) into \(\mathcal S\),
\[
 H^{\top}e_i=UA^{-\top}e_i,
 \qquad Ge_i=UAe_i,
\]
and hence the denominator above equals
\(\|H^{\top}e_i\|_2\|Ge_i\|_2\).  Taking the minimum over witness labels gives the lower bound \(\rho^{\ast}(G)\).  The declared formula for the printed \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)\) is instead the norm product itself; it is therefore not the reciprocal lower bound just derived.
